subject: ventures/ubuntu-agent-server
professional: a senior SRE / Linux platform engineer who runs unattended automation with write access to GitHub (Ansible, systemd, CI bots); first checks: does each headless CLI invocation actually start, does dry-run really do nothing repeatedly costly, can the runner claim an issue on a fresh repo, are the guardrails (kill switch, secret scan, dry_run) tested, does the playbook parse and lint, and does the branch it pushes contain only the agent's change

evidence.correctness: Recomputed against tools the author did not write. (1) FAIL: the real Claude Code CLI (2.1.326 on this box) run with claude.sh's exact flags, `cd /tmp && claude -p "say ok" --output-format stream-json --permission-mode auto`, exits 1 with `Error: When using --print, --output-format=stream-json requires --verbose`; claude.sh:40-43 passes stream-json without --verbose, so every claude run fails before a token. (2) FAIL: an end-to-end harness (fake `gh` keeping issue/label state, a real local bare git origin, a stub codex.sh that edits a file; /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-oss-monorepo/5b82a73b-8972-5197-92b7-4f4eb75fbae4/scratchpad/ubuntu-agent-server/harness.sh) runs the shipped agent_runner.py main() three times with dry_run: true: `tool_runs(clones)= 3 comments= 3 labels_now= ['agent']`. The dry-run branch (agent_runner.py:730-741) only unclaims and never adds a done label, so the same issue is re-cloned, re-run and re-commented on every 10-minute poll (144 tool runs and comments a day), and on a self_directed repo the open self-directed issue stays a candidate forever. (3) PASS: `systemd-analyze calendar '*:0/10' --iterations=3` gives 07:20, 07:30, 07:40, matching the documented every-10-minutes schedule. (4) PASS: harness2.sh (non-dry run, stub tool commits its own change while an upstream commit lands on origin/main mid-run) leaves origin's agent/codex/issue-1 differing from current main only in `a.txt | 1 +`, label `agent:pr-opened`: the sync+fold logic does not revert upstream work. (5) PASS: `claude --help` lists `auto` among --permission-mode choices. (6) PASS: kill switch: with DISABLED present, main() exits 0 with zero gh calls. Two of the four tool paths' core failures are on the primary path (claude broken outright; any dry run burns quota without bound), so 1.
evidence.completeness: Claimed features checked: kill switch works (run, 0 gh calls); fresh clone, branch, per-tool identity, fold, push, PR, labels work end to end in the harness when labels exist; mid-run upstream sync works; secret scan skipped silently when gitleaks absent (as documented); playbook parses (`ansible-playbook playbook.yml --syntax-check` -> `playbook: playbook.yml`). Not working or not done: the claude runner (fails on argument parsing); dry_run loops; no task anywhere creates the agent:in-progress / agent:pr-opened / agent:failed / agent:self-directed labels (`grep -rn 'label create' roles/` is empty), and `gh issue edit --add-label` on a label that does not exist fails, so on a fresh repo claim_issue returns False and nothing is ever worked (harness with labels absent: 0 runs, 0 comments, nothing on GitHub to show why); Docker sandbox and antigravity/opencode paths are self-declared untested; README says nothing has ever run against a real repo or host.
evidence.verification: `cd ventures/ubuntu-agent-server && /usr/bin/python3.13 -m pytest -q tests` -> 43 passed in 1.56 s. Pure helpers are well covered (fold, sync, tier choice, cooldown, docker argv). Four mutants via platform/ci/quality_mutate.py: 2 caught (tier threshold 800 -> 8000; fold reset onto HEAD), 2 SURVIVED, both safety guardrails: inverting `if dry_run:` (agent_runner.py:730, so a dry-run repo pushes and opens PRs) and bypassing the gitleaks result (agent_runner.py:716). process_issue/_process_issue_inner, the code that decides push vs no-push, has no test at all, which is also why the dry-run loop and the missing-label failure were not caught. Runner scripts are only grepped for strings (test_codex_runner_*), never executed against a CLI's argument parser, so the stream-json/--verbose break passed.
evidence.craft: Read agent_runner.py (812 lines), all four runners/*.sh, roles/agent_runner/tasks/main.yml, the systemd templates, Dockerfile, group_vars/all.yml, config/repos.yml, tests. `shellcheck runners/*.sh bootstrap.sh` exit 0; `pyflakes agent_runner.py tests` exit 0; syntax-check clean. Comments are unusually candid about uncertainty. Defects: no label bootstrap; process_issue untested and calls run_id() twice so workspace and log names can differ by a second (agent_runner.py:584-585); pr-create failure labels failed then raises into the broad handler which labels and comments again (763-766 + 592-602); gitleaks installed from 'latest' with no checksum check (tasks/main.yml:37-62); Dockerfile `curl ... install.sh | bash || true` hides an install failure; credential mounts are read-only and omit ~/.claude.json, so a containerised claude is likely unauthenticated (agent_runner.py:124-130).
evidence.claims: No public page (served-copy: `not a published product`), so claims are the README. Unbacked or false: 'Skips any issue already labeled ... so nothing gets worked twice' (false under dry_run, harness above); 'Claude Code and Codex CLI's headless modes are the two on solid, current, primary-source footing' and 'exact headless/permission flags for Claude Code ... checked against each vendor's own current docs' (claude invocation rejected by the CLI); 'tests/ has 28 unit tests' (43); '.github/workflows/ci.yml' (does not exist; the workflow is the repo-level .github/workflows/ubuntu-agent-server-ci.yml); 'the separate Hetzner product box' (retired 2026-10-01, README line 3 says so); 'matching gitops/agents/workers/worker.sh' (tree deleted). Backed: kill-switch behaviour, codex API-key unset and login preflight (codex.sh:52-64), the PR-only/no-merge design, the honest 'never executed against a real repo' disclaimer.
evidence.fitness: The job: the owner provisions a box and lets agents work labelled issues safely. Walked through in the harness: on a repo without the agent:* labels the runner silently does nothing; with labels and the shipped `dry_run: true` codex entry it re-runs the agent every 10 minutes on the same issue, spending the ChatGPT plan quota and posting a comment each time; switching the tool to claude fails every run. An operator following the README's 'watch a few dry runs' advice would get a spam loop and a drained quota before trusting it.
evidence.domain: Against SRE practice for unattended bots: good choices (systemd oneshot + timer so runs cannot overlap, master kill switch enforced by config management, fresh ephemeral clone per run, fine-grained PAT advice, staged-only secret scan, PR-only, Persistent=true). Departures: dry-run is not idempotent (a dry run must leave a marker, e.g. an agent:dry-run label, or it is a load generator); required GitHub labels are not provisioned as code despite the repo's 'everything as code' direction; no integration test of the CLI argv against real binaries (the cheapest check a platform engineer runs: `<cli> --help`/argument parse); unpinned, unverified binary download for the security scanner; issue bodies go verbatim into an autonomous agent's prompt with only the trigger label as the human gate, with no note on prompt injection from non-maintainer issue authors.

defects.what: claude.sh passes --output-format stream-json with -p but no --verbose; Claude Code rejects this with 'requires --verbose' and exit 1, so every claude-tool run fails before starting and the issue is labelled agent:failed

dry_run path unclaims the issue but adds no marker label, so the same issue is re-cloned, re-run by the agent and re-commented on every poll (3 polls -> 3 runs, 3 comments; 144/day at the default schedule), draining plan quota; the shipped monorepo entry is dry_run + self_directed

no task creates the agent:in-progress / agent:pr-opened / agent:failed / agent:self-directed labels; gh issue edit/create with a missing label fails, so on a fresh repo claim_issue returns False and the runner silently never works anything
process_issue/_process_issue_inner (push/no-push, dry_run, secret-scan gate) has no test; mutants inverting dry_run and bypassing gitleaks both survive
README says nothing gets worked twice and that Claude Code's headless flags were checked against vendor docs; both false (dry-run loop; stream-json without --verbose rejected)
README says 28 unit tests (43 now) and points at .github/workflows/ci.yml inside the subject (CI is the repo-level ubuntu-agent-server-ci.yml)
README and codex.sh cite the retired Hetzner product box and the deleted gitops/agents/workers/worker.sh
gitleaks is downloaded from 'latest' with no checksum verification, and the Dockerfile pipes an install script to bash with '|| true', hiding failures in the security-relevant toolchain
run_id() is called separately for workspace and log names, so they can differ by a second and the comment's log path may not match the workspace stamp

verdict: A carefully commented Ansible + systemd agent runner whose pure helpers are well tested (43 pass; sync/fold verified against real git with an upstream commit landing mid-run) and whose playbook parses and lints clean, but the primary paths fail when actually run: the real Claude Code CLI rejects claude.sh's flags ('stream-json requires --verbose'), dry_run re-runs the agent on the same issue every poll (harness: 3 polls, 3 runs, 3 comments), and the GitHub labels the claim step needs are never created, so a fresh repo is silently never worked. The guardrail code (dry_run, secret-scan gate) has no test and two mutants there survive. It does not meet the bar; a senior SRE would not enable it until those three are fixed and the CLI argv is exercised against the real binaries.
